result.title: Learning to Look Beyond Screens: Transferable Visual Observation from GUI Grounding
result.summary: Visual perception is evolving from passive recognition toward active, task-oriented observation. We investigate GUI grounding as a scalable source of spatial supervision for learning observation behaviors that transfer beyond interfaces. We introduce LBS (Look Beyond Screens), a vision-language model trained through supervised initialization on teacher-generated GUI grounding trajectories, followed by reinforcement learning for multi-turn crop-and-inspect decisions. Under fixed inference settings, LBS models based on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3.8-27B consistently improve over their corresponding baselines. Gains beyond supervised fine-tuning transfer to PerceptionBench for both backbones and to HR-Bench and ChartQAPro for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, supporting observation strategies that generalize beyond GUI-specific imitation. Further analysis suggests complementary roles for the two stages: SFT establishes visual inspection primitives, while RL improves their downstream effectiveness. These findings support GUI grounding as a practical supervision paradigm for transferable active visual perception and broader multimodal reasoning. Our code and model are publicly available at https://github.com/inclusionAI/UI-Venus/tree/LBS and https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/LBS-27B, respectively.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将 GUI grounding 作为可扩展的空间监督来源，提出 LBS：先由教师生成的 grounding 轨迹做监督初始化，再用强化学习训练多轮「裁剪—检查」的主动观察策略，并在多个感知基准上验证其可迁移性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其多轮裁剪取证与观察原语训练直接对应 LVR 中 LOOK 行为、视觉证据获取与选择，可供核查主动感知策略能否为 latent 推理提供更有效的视觉输入及相应的计算成本。
